facts.text: Taylorsville today blends two historic communities, Taylorsville and Bennion, that merged into a single city in 1996.
Two railroads once crisscrossed the area: the Rio Grande and Western reached Bingham Junction, while the Bingham‑Garfield Railroad arrived in 1910.
The city sits on an alluvial plain formed by erosion of the Wasatch and Oquirrh Mountains, stretching across the Salt Lake Valley.
Beneath the streets lies more than a kilometer of unconsolidated sand, clay, and rock, a reminder of the valley’s ancient lake beds.
Indigenous Fremont people hunted and gathered along the Jordan River in this valley over a thousand years ago.
In the late 1800s, a local brass band emerged from the community’s musicians, reflecting the town’s early cultural life.
